messages:
ellie: Heads-up: central1 control plane acting up. Console returns 503 for ~30% of sessions, API token verification failing intermittently, and the GPU scheduler reports a sudden drop in available GPUs (pools showing -40%).

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1287 · priority P1 · paging oncall-infra

raj: I'm looking at the control-plane logs now. Not seeing obvious auth DB errors but there are a bunch of protobuf timeout warnings from config-rollout service.

maria: provisioner-agent in central1 is spiking restarts. kube output: 
```
$ kubectl get pods -n infra -o wide | grep provisioner
provisioner-agent-0   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   5   18m
provisioner-agent-1   1/1 Running           0   1h
```

jordan: scheduler metric stream shows KV cache misses + leader elections around same time. Could be etcd lag or network flapping to control-plane nodes.

oncall-infra: I'm going to start a controlled traffic shift to west2. Plan: 10% increments every 3m, monitor 200/503 ratio and auth error rate. Will also enable console read-only mode.

ellie: +1 to read-only. Can someone flip the flag and post command?

kevin: done — toggled feature flag: console.readonly -> true. UI now returns 503 for write endpoints but loads for viewing.

opsbot: Traffic shift initiated: central1 -> west2, step 1: 10% (timestamp 1929123512)

raj: FYI I restarted provisioner-agent-0 (kubectl rollout restart daemonset/provisioner-agent -n infra). Monitoring pod restart backoff. If it re-crashes, collect stack dump.

maria: stack trace looks like a race during GPU allocation: "panic: nil pointer deref" inside scheduler allocator after an unsuccessful cache sync. Attaching snippet: 
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
#0 github.com/redwood/provisioner.allocGPU+0x12f
#1 ...
```

jordan: Starting manual warm-up in west2: spinning up 8 extra GPU workers to absorb traffic. Also enabling prefix caching for hot routes.

oncall-infra: Step 2 traffic shift -> 30% (timestamp 1929123560). Auth error rate down from 6.2% -> 1.3% after step 2.

kevin: Also disabled scheduled config-rollout job to stop further leader churn (system config-rollout cron -> paused).

ellie: Good catch. Any cost impact estimate from spinning additional GPUs in west2? Ops wants a heads-up.

jordan: Short term bump ~ +$1.2k/hr if we keep 8 extra p4s, but we can scale down once steady.

opsbot: Provisioner-agent-0 back to Running (timestamp 1929123595). No new crashes in 4m.

raj: Confirming etcd latencies are back to normal after network route flaps resolved by network team (they applied a config to core-router). No evidence of data corruption.

oncall-infra: Step 3 traffic shift -> 60% (timestamp 1929123610). Console write paths still routed to central1 fallback; read-only remains enforced.

ellie: Is there risk of rollback causing stuck model rollouts? Any pinned version routing we should watch?

jordan: We paused rollouts earlier. No automated rollouts running; manual rollouts are blocked until control plane is healthy.

kevin: I'll open an ops-billing ticket to authorize temporary spend for the extra workers.

opsbot: Status update posted to status.redwood.com: "Partial degradation in central1 control plane impacting console writes and provisioning. Traffic shifting to west2."
